blocks.text: 1. Positional Embeddings
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446158606-735581339.png

Sentence embeddings' own closing recap, already covered in Sentence Embeddings, pointed forward here. Positional Embeddings, addressing how order information gets reintroduced into these representations, close out this module.
They genuinely encode each token's own position directly into its own vector, a genuinely targeted fix explored throughout this topic.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to sentence embeddings' own closing recap, already covered in Sentence Embeddings. Positional embeddings were genuinely previewed there as reintroducing order information, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely gives it the complete, dedicated treatment already promised, exploring every detail already hinted at generally in that earlier topic.
3. The Order Lost Problem
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446158606-768787816.png

This connects back to averaging losing all word order information, already covered in Sentence Embeddings. This same order-blindness genuinely affects several embedding approaches already covered across this module.
The genuinely same set of words in a genuinely different order still produces the exact same bag of vectors, a genuinely real, recurring gap explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Attention Has No Built In Order

blocks.alt: Attention Has No Built In Order
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446158606-805396880.png

This connects back to self-attention, already covered generally elsewhere in this course. Attention genuinely compares every token against every other token equally, regardless of where each one sits in the sequence.
This happens with genuinely no inherent notion of which token came first, second, or last, a genuinely specific gap that positional embeddings, already covered in this topic, exist to fill.
5. Adding Position To Token Embeddings
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446158607-972010368.png
This connects back to attention having no built-in order, already covered in this topic. The genuinely standard fix adds a separate position vector directly onto each token's own embedding.
So the genuinely combined vector now carries both word meaning and word position together, a genuinely simple, additive mechanism explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This additive mechanism, already covered in this topic, directly explains why transformer architectures, already covered generally elsewhere in this course, need positional embeddings even though attention itself carries no order.

blocks.text: 6. Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446158972-843778125.png
This connects back to adding position to token embeddings, already covered in this topic. One genuinely classic scheme uses sine and cosine waves of different frequencies to encode each position.

This produces a genuinely unique, smoothly varying pattern for every individual position, a genuinely elegant, fixed formula requiring no additional training explored throughout the rest of this topic.
7. Learned Positional Embeddings
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446158974-668933934.png
This connects back to sinusoidal positional encoding, already covered in this topic. An alternative genuinely learns a separate position vector for each position during training.

This happens rather than computing it from a fixed sine and cosine formula, already covered here, letting the model genuinely adapt its own position vectors to whatever pattern the training data actually needs.

blocks.text: 8. Relative Positional Encoding
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446158975-595355024.png

This connects back to learned positional embeddings, already covered in this topic. A genuinely different family encodes the relative distance between token pairs instead of each token's own absolute position.

This happens rather than each token's own genuinely fixed, absolute position in the sequence, a genuinely useful property when relationships between nearby tokens matter more than their exact overall position.
9. Recognizing Why Positional Embeddings Are Genuinely Necessary
This connects back to attention having no built-in order, already covered in this topic. Positional embeddings, already covered in this topic, directly restore that missing order signal.

This connects back to RNNs, already covered generally elsewhere in this course, processing tokens one at a time. RNNs, already covered, get order for genuinely free from their own sequential processing instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates sinusoidal positional encoding, already covered in this topic, computing genuinely unique position vectors for a short sequence.

code.content:
import math

def positional_encoding(position, dim=4):
    # already covered as sine and cosine waves of different frequencies in this topic
    vector = []
    for i in range(dim):
        frequency = 1 / (10000 ** (2 * (i // 2) / dim))
        if i % 2 == 0:
            vector.append(round(math.sin(position * frequency), 3))
        else:
            vector.append(round(math.cos(position * frequency), 3))
    return vector

sentence = ["the", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]

print("Positional vectors (already covered as sinusoidal positional encoding in this topic):")
for pos, word in enumerate(sentence):
    pe = positional_encoding(pos)
    print(f"  Position {pos} ('{word}'): {pe}")

# already covered as the order lost problem in this topic
print("\nNote: 'the' appears at position 0 and position 4, and genuinely gets two different")
print("positional vectors each time, even though the word embedding itself stays the same")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the exact same word receiving two genuinely different positional vectors depending on where it sits in the sentence, directly solving the order lost problem already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Embeddings: Module Complete

items: Positional embeddings encode each token's own position directly into its own vector.
Several embedding approaches covered across this module lose all word order information.
Attention compares every token against every other equally, with no inherent notion of order.
The standard fix adds a separate position vector directly onto each token's own embedding.
Sinusoidal positional encoding uses sine and cosine waves to produce a unique pattern per position.
Learned positional embeddings instead learn a separate vector per position during training.
Relative positional encoding encodes the distance between token pairs, not absolute position.
RNNs get order for free from sequential processing; attention-based models need positional embeddings.
